chunks: Ibn al-Mughīrah narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
The diyah for the hand, when it is cut off, is fifty camels. As for wounds less than complete severance, two just individuals among you shall judge regarding them.
And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed—then they are the disbelievers.

key_terms.بِمَا أَنْزَلَ ٱللَّهُ: that which Allah has revealed as the basis of judgment
key_terms.جُرُوحًا دُونَ ٱلِٱصْطِلَامِ: wounds less than complete severance or total amputation
key_terms.خَمْسُونَ مِنَ ٱلْإِبِلِ: fifty camels as the fixed legal compensation
key_terms.دِيَةُ ٱلْيَدِ: the prescribed blood money for injury to a hand
key_terms.ذَوَا عَدْلٍ: two just persons qualified to give judgment

ai.seo_question: What is the diyah for a severed hand, and how are lesser wounds judged in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on diyah, stating that the compensation for a severed hand is fifty camels. For injuries less than complete amputation, the matter is to be assessed by two just persons. It concludes by citing a Qur'anic principle emphasizing judgment according to what Allah has revealed.
